official.deadline_note: Merit scholarships: applications 1-31 October 2026. Study grants run separate windows: 1-20 September 2026 and a second phase 2-22 October 2026. Both are annual award cycles administered by JKU's Teaching and Studies Organization.
official.status_note: The 2026 merit scholarship application window is open from October 1, 2026 to October 31, 2026; the second study-grant window runs October 2-22, 2026.
benefits: The amount of a merit-based scholarship ranges from €750 to €1,500, paid out in a single lump sum upon award of the scholarship.
A study grant may not be less than €750 but cannot exceed €3,600.
Study grants can also be awarded in addition to a merit scholarship.
The scholarships are awarded annually and funds have been made available by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Science, Research and the Economy.
Study grants help fund costs incurred to prepare the groundwork of a thesis or dissertation that are not covered by the supervising institute's budget or by other sources.
eligibility: Merit scholarships: students who completed their degree program in the allotted time with an average GPA of no less than 2.0.
Merit scholarships are awarded in recognition of outstanding academic achievement.
Study grants: unfinished academic and scientific work (Diploma degree theses, Master's theses, and doctoral dissertations) that is a required part of an academic degree program.
No citizenship or residency requirement is published for these university awards.
requirements: Applications can only be accepted via the online form, which is available only in German.
For merit scholarships, the calculation sheet (Berechnungsblatt) should be uploaded as a PDF file in the application form to expedite review.
For study grants, a cost calculation and budget (Kostenaufstellung und Finanzierungsplan) form must be completed.
The degree program must have been completed within the allotted time (merit route).
documents: Online application form (German only) submitted through JKU's forms portal
Calculation sheet for the merit scholarship, uploaded as PDF
Cost calculation and budget form for study grants
The submitted form can be saved or exported (printer icon) as confirmation of submission
selection_criteria: Merit scholarships: outstanding academic achievement, with an average GPA of no less than 2.0 and completion of the degree program in the allotted time.
Study grants: demonstrated thesis/dissertation costs not covered by the supervising institute's budget or other sources.
After the application deadline, the responsible working groups render a decision on how the scholarships will be awarded.
All applicants receive notification of the outcome regarding their scholarship application by e-mail.
coverage: Merit scholarship: a one-off recognition payment for outstanding academic achievement (€750-€1,500 lump sum).
Study grant: a one-off payment (€750-€3,600) toward the costs of preparing a thesis or dissertation not covered elsewhere.
Neither award is published as covering tuition fees, living costs, or travel.
application_method: Apply through the online form linked from the JKU scholarship pages (German only; available only during the annual application window).
Upload the calculation sheet as a PDF within the form to speed up processing.
After submitting, export/save the form via the printer icon as confirmation of submission.
official.application_route: Online application form on JKU's forms portal (German only) during the annual window: 1-31 October 2026 for merit scholarships; September and October windows for study grants.
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship or residency requirement published.
official.international_eligibility: No nationality restriction published; the merit criteria apply to students of JKU degree programs, so enrolled international students can apply.
official.research_requirement: Study grants require unfinished thesis or dissertation work (Diploma degree thesis, Master's thesis, or doctoral dissertation) that is a required part of an academic degree program.
official.duration: One-off lump-sum payment; scholarships are awarded annually.
official.description: JKU awards merit scholarships in recognition of outstanding academic achievement, ranging from €750 to €1,500 and paid in a single lump sum, to students who completed their degree program in the allotted time with an average GPA of at least 2.0. Study grants of €750 to €3,600 fund unfinished Diploma, Master's, or doctoral thesis work, and can be combined with a merit scholarship. Both are funded from allocations of the Austrian Federal Ministry of Science, Research and the Economy.
official.program_type: University merit scholarship and study grant (for enrolled students)

not_confirmed: explicit international-student eligibility wording (no nationality restriction is published either way)
verification.notes: Amounts (€750-€1,500 merit, €750-€3,600 study grants), the lump-sum payment rule, the 2026 windows (merit 1-31 Oct; grants 1-20 Sep and 2-22 Oct), GPA 2.0 and on-time completion criteria, and the German-only online route were confirmed on JKU's own English and German pages. JKU's pages publish no tuition waiver, living-cost, or travel coverage for these awards, so the catalogue's earlier 'tuition fee waiver' wording is not supported and was dropped.

applicant_utility.summary: These are internal awards for students already enrolled at JKU, not entrance scholarships, so there is nothing to apply for before you are studying in Linz. The merit route hinges on finishing your degree within the standard time with an average grade of at least 2.0, and the application form exists only in German even though the information pages are in English. The money arrives as a single lump sum and covers neither tuition nor living costs, so treat it as a bonus on top of your own funding and the Austrian Studienbeihilfe rather than a study budget.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled JKU students, including internationals, who finished on time with strong grades, and thesis writers whose project costs their supervising institute will not cover.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify you completed (or will complete) the degree within the allotted time with an average GPA of at least 2.0 before the 1-31 October 2026 merit window opens.
Prepare the calculation sheet (Berechnungsblatt) in advance and keep a PDF ready to upload inside the form.
Complete the German-only online form inside the window and export the confirmation via the printer icon as proof of submission.
For thesis-stage applicants, gather the cost breakdown showing which costs the supervising institute will not cover, for the study-grant window.
Track the separate study-grant windows (1-20 September and 2-22 October 2026) if you are between the merit categories.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the one-month window: awards are annual, so a missed deadline means waiting until the next cycle.
An average grade below 2.0 or overrunning the allotted study time, which removes the merit route entirely.
Submitting without the required calculation sheet, which slows or stalls review.
Assuming this is a tuition waiver or a monthly stipend and budgeting as if living costs were covered.
Applying as a prospective or not-yet-enrolled student; these rewards go to current JKU students only.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, rent, living expenses, insurance, and travel are not covered; applicants fund these themselves, for example via the Austrian Study Grant Authority (stipendium.at), which JKU's pages point to for additional support.
document_audit: The calculation sheet must be uploaded as a PDF inside the online form, not sent separately by email.
The application form is German-only even though the program pages are published in English.
No submission confirmation is emailed at the time of applying; only the exported form serves as proof until the decision notification arrives.
alerts: The 2026 merit scholarship window closes 31 October 2026 and reopens only with the next annual cycle.
Study grants have two windows; the second one closes 22 October 2026.
Study grants stack with merit scholarships, so a thesis writer in the final phase can pursue both.
Contact for questions is the Teaching and Studies Organization (stipendium@jku.at, +43 732 2468 3103), with phone hours Monday and Wednesday 10:00-12:00 only.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill the German-only online form during the window, upload the calculation sheet as PDF, submit, export the confirmation, then await the working groups' decision by email.
